title: Further Development

spine.markdown: The next step will be to test InterText with human readers. It will admittedly be an uphill battle to convince human readers to change their reading practice significantly. The success of the e-reader, for example, was precisely that it did not require significant change to the linear experience of reading (Baron 2015).

fundEntries.title: Threads through the fund
fundEntries.useWhen: A reader asks what new forms of reading the system might offer.
fundEntries.markdown: Units of the fund can already be grouped into a named sequence. The text does not yet offer such a sequence to the reader as a path, but it could: a line of examples, an objection pursued across several sections, or a series of contributions from readers.

fundEntries.title: An author's editor online
fundEntries.useWhen: A reader asks how an author would manage an evolving text in practice, or how others could use the system.
fundEntries.markdown: The author's editor is kept off the public site until it can be secured and until there is a policy for the manuscript and the records of origin it holds. An editor available online would allow an author to follow an evolving text as it changes, and would allow other authors to adapt their own texts for the system, which is designed to carry more than one.
